newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GPG says considering share reduction.
newsitem.headline: GPG says considering share reduction.

text.p: Guiness Peat Group Plc said in a release to the New Zealand Stock Exchange on Wednesday that it would "during the current term" be considering proposals to reduce the number of shares in issue.
"A recommendation will be made to shareholders in due course," the company said.
GPG said that in the past it had an informal commitment to annual 1 for 10 rights and bonus issues but this year decided not to make a rights issue.
"The group is in a strong position and the fiscal discipline of not unnecessarily expanding the capital base will be of benefit to shareholders."
GPG reported a 19.14 million pound net profit in the year to December 31, up from 14.71 million.

Contributing much of the profit for the period was the sale of shares in Physicians Insurance Co. Of Ohio (PICO) (in conjunction with the Citation Insurance merger) and settlement of the Ampolex litigation, GPG said.
GPG said the sale of shares was simply a prudent reduction in its exposure to the uncertainties of the U.S. market when there was the opportunity to do so on a reasonably favourable basis.
"We are still the largest stockholder in the new PICO Holdings and it remains an important investment for us."
GPG said the merits of a negotiated commercial settlement over Ampolex far outweighed the prospect of up to several more years of complex legal proceedings.

Since balance date, it had become increasingly clear its offer for The Ballarat Brewing Co was unlikely to succeed on mutually acceptable terms, so it sold its existing shareholding to the competing bidder, Foster Brewing.
GPG said its main subsidiary, Tyndall Australia continued to make good progress and should receive a further boost this year with the integration of the recently acquired Oceanic Assurance.
In New Zealand, Turners & Growers showed "a marked recovery in earnings" and The Colonial Motor Co had achieved all that was hoped when GPG became the major shareholder in 1995.
The NZ Guardian Trust Co provided a good base for expansion in the funds management industry, GPG said.
GPG said it was intended shortly to divest two listed subsidiaries - ASC Ltd and Metals Exploration.

"We propose to acquire full ownership of ASC's assets at a small discount to market, in exchange for a cash payment to minority shareholders and our 83 percent interest in Metals Exploration will be sold on a somewhat similar basis."
